prompts: This is an exercise. Do not give away solutions; use https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/01_tabular_data_exploration_sol_01.html only to craft hints and guiding questions. This exercise applies exploratory data analysis skills from the preceding instructional notebook to a new dataset: penguins classified by species based on two numerical body measurements, culmen length and culmen depth. Key learning objectives are: (1) identifying features and target in a new dataset; (2) loading and inspecting a DataFrame with pandas; (3) using value_counts to summarize the class distribution of the 'Species' target column; (4) plotting histograms of numerical features and a seaborn.pairplot colored by species to visually assess class separability. Expected outputs include: penguins loaded as a DataFrame from penguins_classification.csv, a head() display, value_counts() on 'Species' (Adelie: 151, Gentoo: 123, Chinstrap: 68), histograms of 'Culmen Length (mm)' and 'Culmen Depth (mm)', and a pairplot with hue='Species'. The final question asks students to reason qualitatively about separability. When students struggle with seaborn.pairplot, guide them to identify which parameters are mandatory (the DataFrame and hue) versus purely cosmetic (alpha, height, diag_kind), and encourage them to consult the seaborn documentation or experiment by removing optional parameters one at a time. If asked about more information on the dataset, refer to https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/trees_dataset.html
